verses.text: The LORD was angry with Israel again. He moved David against them and told him, “Go count the people of Israel and Judah.”
The king told Joab, his army commander, “Travel through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people so I know how many there are.”
Joab told the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the people a hundred times over and let my lord the king see it. But why do you want to do this?”
The king overruled Joab and the army commanders. So they left the king and went to count the people of Israel.
They crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer on the right side of the city in the middle of the valley of Gad, then went toward Jazer.
They came to Gilead and the land of Tahtim Hodshi, then went on to Dan Jaan and around to Sidon.
They went to the fortress of Tyre and to all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Then they headed south into Judah, ending at Beersheba.
After traveling throughout the land, they returned to Jerusalem nine months and twenty days later.
Joab reported the census totals to the king. Israel had eight hundred thousand warriors who could draw a sword, and Judah had five hundred thousand men.
After he counted the people, David's conscience struck him. He said to the LORD, “I've sinned badly by doing this. Please take away my guilt, LORD. I've acted like a fool.”
When David got up the next morning, the LORD gave this message to Gad the prophet, David's seer:
“Go tell David, ‘The LORD says: I'm putting three choices before you. Choose one, and I'll bring it upon you.’”

Gad came to David and asked, “Will you have seven years of famine in your land? Will you spend three months running while your enemies chase you? Or will your land face three days of plague? Think about it and tell me what answer to take back to the one who sent me.”
David answered Gad, “I'm in deep trouble. Let us fall into the LORD's hands, because his mercy is great. Please don't let me fall into human hands.”
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the appointed time. Seventy thousand people died from Dan to Beersheba.

When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented and told the angel striking the people, “That's enough. Pull back your hand.” The LORD's angel was beside the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

When David saw the angel striking the people, he said to the LORD, “I'm the one who sinned and did wrong. But these sheep, what have they done? Please turn your hand against me and my father's family.”
That day Gad came to David and told him, “Go up to the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite and build an altar to the LORD there.”
David went up as Gad told him, just as the LORD had commanded.
Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him. He went out and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
Araunah asked, “Why has my lord the king come to see his servant?” David replied, “To buy your threshing floor and build an altar to the LORD, so the plague will stop killing the people.”
Araunah told David, “My lord the king can take whatever he wants to offer. Here are the cattle for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
Your Majesty, I give it all to you. May the LORD your God accept you.”
But the king answered Araunah, “No. I'll pay you for it. I won't offer the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
David built an altar there to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The LORD answered the plea for the land, and the plague that had struck Israel ended.
